description: Exobiology: genus, species, biome predictions, sample values

entries.content: Exobiology samples are collected using the Genetic Sampler tool. Three samples from distinct colonies of the same species are required to complete analysis. Samples must be collected from colonies separated by a minimum distance (the Colonial Range), which is species-specific. The journal records each sample via the ScanOrganic event with ScanType values of Log, Sample, and Analyse.

entries.topic: Signal Counts and Genera Are Journal Facts, Not Predictions
entries.content: After a Detailed Surface Scanner map, Elite reports the number of biological signals on a body in SAASignalsFound.Signals[] with Type '$SAA_SignalType_Biological;' and a Count. In Odyssey the same event also carries a Genuses[] array naming which genera are present. Both are observed facts and must be surfaced as such. Only the species within a genus, and the credit value of a sample, require prediction or reference estimation. A tool that predicts a signal count when the journal already reported one is discarding a fact in favour of a guess.
entries._justification: Phase 13 exobiology slice. Records the fact/prediction boundary so future work reads SAASignalsFound before reaching for a condition matcher.

entries.content: Where a biological organism can occur in Elite is governed by conditions Frontier has never published. What exists instead is community-derived empirical mechanics: rules reconstructed by long-running research groups from large numbers of observed samples. OmniCOVAS treats those as operational truth for prediction only, and never describes them as Frontier-published spawn rules. Occurrence is evaluated at SPECIES level, and within a species it is evaluated as a set of alternative rule BRANCHES rather than one band per dimension. A species occurs where at least one whole branch is satisfied, and the predicates inside a branch are correlated: the same species can occur under one atmosphere on one body class at one gravity range, and under a different atmosphere on a different body class at a different range. Combining those into a single species-wide list would invent pairings no source rule allows, so OmniCOVAS does not do it. A species is excluded only when every one of its branches is definitively ruled out. The dimensions that can gate a branch include body class, atmosphere type, atmospheric composition, surface temperature, surface gravity, atmospheric pressure, volcanism and its material, parent star class, orbital period, galactic region, nebula proximity, and explicit location restrictions. Not all of those are observable from a Commander's own journal. Where a branch depends on one that is not, OmniCOVAS reports that species as undecided rather than treating it as a match, so an unknown is never converted into a candidate. Gravity has no universal ceiling: tolerances range from roughly 0.025g to 0.7g, and Stratum Tectonicas alone reaches more than double the ~0.28g figure once assumed to apply to everything. A rule match means the body's recorded conditions are consistent with that species. It is a candidate, never a confirmation that anything is present. Biological signal counts and the genera named by the journal after a surface scan are observed facts and always outrank prediction; where the journal has already named the genera on a body, OmniCOVAS shows those and predicts nothing. These rules can be wrong, and a Commander's own telemetry is what proves it. A confirmed ScanOrganic establishes that the species was present under the conditions the journal recorded for that body, so a rule that called that body impossible is false or incomplete. OmniCOVAS detects that case, records the contradiction with the ruleset version that produced it, and suspends the falsified exclusion locally so it cannot keep generating false negatives. It does not rewrite the community rule: the canonical value is preserved and the contradiction is flagged for review. One observation falsifies a bound but does not establish the replacement bound, so the suspended predicate becomes Unknown rather than taking the observed value, and an observed range is recorded as an observed envelope rather than a spawn limit. These rules change with balance patches. This entry describes how prediction works; it is not the rules themselves. The machine source of truth is the structured ruleset shipped at omnicovas/data/exobiology_species_ruleset.json, which holds the 91 species-level records and their 225 rule branches that actually drive candidate matching.
entries.source: Community-derived empirical mechanics, independently normalised from EDMC-BioScan's published ruleset (latest release v2.12.2, read at master revision 5f0d2e445a95681bf2e85223f883d5c552a7726b), Canonn Research's per-genus observation distributions, and the Deep Space Network conditions reference; cross-checked between sources, disagreements recorded rather than resolved, independently verified before implementation, and re-audited species-by-species and branch-by-branch. Documented counterexamples that falsify a rule are recorded in EXOBIOLOGY_KNOWN_COUNTEREXAMPLES.md. Not Frontier-published. Per-branch source attribution, the body-class re-audit and the open source disagreements are preserved under evidence/research/exobiology-ruleset-20260817/.
entries._justification: Phase 13 exobiology accuracy hardening. Rewritten because the previous wording described occurrence as one band per dimension per species, which is how the flattened dataset worked and is not how the underlying rules work: the maintained source has always carried alternative correlated branches, and flattening them admitted 67 body/atmosphere combinations no rule allows while excluding 34 that are real. Now describes branch evaluation, and describes the Rule Sentinel because a Commander needs to know that their own samples can overturn a rule, that doing so suspends the rule locally rather than rewriting it, and that a suspended bound becomes Unknown rather than the value they happened to observe. Still deliberately no per-species table here - that would recreate the hand-maintained duplicate this reconciliation exists to remove. needs_review stays cleared: the dataset behind it is independently verified and hash-asserted by test. Confidence stays medium because the underlying sources remain community observation rather than published values, several cross-source disagreements remain open and disclosed, one shipped rule is recorded as falsified with no defensible replacement, and one species' body class is still genuinely unknown.

entries.content: Exobiology payouts vary enormously by genus and species, from roughly 1 million credits for common Bacterium variants to roughly 19-20 million for the highest-value species such as Stratum Tectonicas. A first-logged bonus (historically an additional multiple of base value) applies when the Commander is the first to register that species. Actual credits received are always reported by the journal in SellOrganicData BioData[] Value and Bonus fields, and those observed values must always take precedence over any reference figure. Reference values are for pre-sale expectation only, change with balance patches, and must never be added to a figure describing money already received.
entries.source: community value tables and in-game observation; not Frontier-published
entries._justification: Phase 13 exobiology value slice. Ranges only, never per-species precision, because the source does not support precision and a wrong exact figure reads as authoritative. SellOrganicData observed values outrank this entry wherever both exist.
